articles.title: India-NZ FTA in force: Over half of New Zealand’s exports to India now tariff-free, Wellington also eyes B - The Economic Times
articles.summary: India-NZ FTA in force: Over half of New Zealand’s exports to India now tariff-free, Wellington also eyes B  The Economic Times
articles.full_text:
Synopsis
New Zealand is working to strengthen trade relations with Brazil and Canada in response to economic uncertainties. The country expects to complete the first New Zealand-Brazil Trade and Investment Dialogue after upcoming elections. A new free trade agreement with India has been implemented, making more than half of exports tariff-free. The agreement will benefit various products, including sheep meat and wool, as well as local businesses.
Also read: India-New Zealand FTA to kick in October 20, opening market opportunities for exporters
From Tuesday more than half of New Zealand's exports to India are tariff-free and this will rise to 82% over time. Tariffs have been removed on products including sheep meat, wool and coal, while apples, kiwifruit and milk albumins will receive preferential quota access. "The gains go well beyond exports. They reach suppliers, local businesses and the towns that depend on them," McClay said.
The statement said New Zealand and Brazil would establish a Trade and Investment Dialogue covering trade, investment, World Trade Organization reform and possible future trade negotiations.
New Zealand and Canada would create an annual dialogue between senior officials, followed by annual trade-minister meetings.

articles.title: Trump waives Russia sanctions, easing India’s energy concerns as US trade deal nears - The Economic Times
articles.summary: Trump waives Russia sanctions, easing India’s energy concerns as US trade deal nears  The Economic Times
articles.full_text:
Synopsis
US President Donald Trump waived key Russian sanctions which may enhance trade relations with India. This decision is expected to provide negotiating space for a potential trade deal. India, one of the largest importers of Russian oil, faces challenges due to declining imports. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is visiting India to discuss cooperation on this matter. The waiver could help India secure more favorable tariffs while stabilizing energy policies.
Trump said the waiver was in the national interest of the United States.
The legislation would have exposed Indian goods to stiff tariffs of up to 100% as India is one of the five largest importers of Russian oil and posed a challenge for the Asian nation's energy policies.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration warned last month the new tariff measures on Russia could hurt bilateral ties, adding to diplomatic strain and trade uncertainty.
RUBIO SAYS TRADE DEAL 'VERY CLOSE'
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who arrives in India on Tuesday, said trade talks with New Delhi were a consideration for Trump's decision.
"We are trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now and we are very close to doing that. So, that's one of the things we take into consideration when the President makes a decision about national security waivers," Rubio told reporters in Uzbekistan on Monday.
India is the world's third-largest oil importer and consumer. Earlier this year, Russia accounted for nearly half of the country's oil imports, but purchases fell in August and continue to decline.
Persistently cutting Russian oil imports to avoid new US tariffs risks pushing up fuel prices ahead of regional elections in India, or straining government finances.
"For some countries it is very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources," Rubio said.
Rubio's two-day visit to India will include a meeting with foreign minister S. Jaishankar on Tuesday to discuss bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade and investment, and defence.
A trade deal between India and the United States has been in the making for months but could not be finalised as talks stalled in part due to complications from the new tariff threat.
A trade deal has also been held back because Washington is yet to complete a Section 301 trade investigation into several nations, including India, over alleged excess manufacturing capacity. Section 301 is a US trade law that allows retaliation against unfair foreign trade practices.
Earlier this month, India joined a US-led initiative to act against structural overcapacity, along with a few other nations.
Trade officials in New Delhi last week said an agreement with the US was nearly done and expressed optimism over securing a tariff lower than those of competing countries - a longstanding Indian expectation from the deal.
"It (the waiver) provides an important opening and at a critical moment" after renewed tensions over the sanctions bill and new US visa policies had put the relationship "in danger of falling into even harder times," Kugelman said.
